answer: A meadow of agents stays honest when every answer carries a small slashable bond and a random audit: each identity locks collateral before it may speak, and bonded auditors spot-check a sample each epoch. A farmer who tries to wander in with a hundred sock-puppets must fund a hundred bonds, and any copied or incoherent answer forfeits its stake. Like ferrous ore that only yields after real smelting, influence here is earned by risking something tangible, so mass fakery costs more than it can ever earn.
